To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the most important factor in reading comprehension is vocabulary, (b) vocabulary is best acquired by reading, and (c) the best way to improve reading comprehension is to increase vocabulary.

(a) the more you read, the better a reader you become; (b) you need to read a variety of materials, not just textbooks, to become a good reader; (c) the better your vocabulary, the better your reading comprehension; (d) you need to be able to understand what you read, not just to decode it, to become a successful reader;

(1) the reading comprehension of students who read in their native language is better than the reading comprehension of second language learners, (2) second language reading comprehension is related to second language listening comprehension, (3) the reading comprehension skills of second language learners are related to their knowledge of English vocabulary and grammar, (4) the reading comprehension skill of second language learners is related to their ability to read for meaning, and (5) the reading comprehension abilities of second language learners vary according to their proficiency

reading is a complex and dynamic process which is not yet completely understood.

the research on reading in a first or second language has been very fruitful and is continuing to produce new knowledge and new insights into the nature of reading and how it can best be taught.

second language readers are different from first language readers in that they are not only acquiring new content but also a new system of language.
reading research and practice has changed in many ways over the past 25 years, and that there is much to be learned and applied to second language reading instruction.
reading research has been expanding and changing, and that the implications of this research are still not well understood by many teachers.

reading is an interactive process.
